facts.fact_text: The applicant is an independent journalist.
The applicant is the chairman of the Institute for Reporters' Freedom and Safety (IRFS), a non-governmental organisation specialising in the protection of journalists' rights.
On 14 June 2008 a group called the 'Che Guevara Fan Club' held a gathering at a private café in Baku to celebrate the eightieth anniversary of the birth of Che Guevara.
There were about twenty-five attendees at the gathering held by the 'Che Guevara Fan Club' on 14 June 2008.
The applicant attended the gathering held by the 'Che Guevara Fan Club' on 14 June 2008, accompanied by two colleagues from the Institute for Reporters' Freedom and Safety (IRFS), R.A. and M.H.
Approximately thirty minutes after the gathering began on 14 June 2008, about thirty police officers entered the café.
The police officers who entered the café on 14 June 2008 suspended the gathering and announced that they were going to take the attendees to the police station.

In response to the applicant's actions, one of the police officers, who was apparently in charge of the intervention on 14 June 2008, ordered other police officers to take the applicant to the police station.
According to the applicant, he was taken to a police car by four police officers on 14 June 2008, who used force against him.

After his arrival at the police station on 14 June 2008, the applicant was separated from the others who had been arrested and was taken to the office of the Deputy Head of Nasimi District Police Station no. 22, A.K.
At around 4 p.m. on 14 June 2008, two police officers accompanied the applicant to the door leading out of the police station.
The café where the gathering was held on 14 June 2008 was located in the basement of a building in the city centre of Baku.

According to the Government, on 14 June 2008 the police intervened in the gathering at the café on the basis of a complaint from people living in the neighbourhood of the café, who complained about noise and the behaviour of those attending.

The spokesman for the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Azerbaijan, E.Z., stated that on 14 June 2008 a group of people held an unauthorised gathering at a café and the police requested the interruption of the unauthorised gathering.

The spokesman for the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Azerbaijan, E.Z., stated that on 14 June 2008 a group of people held an unauthorised gathering at a café and the police requested the interruption of the unauthorised gathering.
The Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009 found that the police intervention had been lawful, since the gathering at the café in the city centre disturbed other people present.

Article 7 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 of Azerbaijan provides that any restriction on freedom of assembly may be put in place only by law and for the purposes of protecting interests necessary in a democratic society, including: protection of the interests of public and state security; preventing the disturbance of public order; prevention of disorder or crime; protection of the health of the population; protection of morals; and protection of the rights and freedoms of others.
The café where the gathering was held on 14 June 2008 was located in the basement of a building in the city centre of Baku.
There were about twenty-five attendees at the gathering held by the 'Che Guevara Fan Club' on 14 June 2008.
Approximately thirty minutes after the gathering began on 14 June 2008, about thirty police officers entered the café.
The police officers who entered the café on 14 June 2008 suspended the gathering and announced that they were going to take the attendees to the police station.
The applicant identified himself to the police officers, informing them that he was a journalist and the chairman of the Institute for Reporters' Freedom and Safety (IRFS).

The applicant had with him his identity card and the card confirming that he was the chairman of the Institute for Reporters' Freedom and Safety (IRFS) at the time of the police intervention on 14 June 2008.
The applicant asked the police officers to identify themselves and to release his arrested colleagues on 14 June 2008.
According to the applicant, he was taken to a police car by four police officers on 14 June 2008, who used force against him.
According to the applicant, the four police officers who took him to the police car on 14 June 2008 punched and kicked him in the stomach.
Four police officers entered the room of the Deputy Head of Nasimi District Police Station no. 22, A.K., and threatened the applicant in the presence of A.K. on 14 June 2008.
According to the applicant, police officer O.A. pushed down the applicant's head by pressing on the back of his neck so that his head hit the table on 14 June 2008.
According to the applicant, police officer O.A. struck the applicant in the neck with his elbow on 14 June 2008, as a result of which the applicant lost consciousness.
At around 4 p.m. on 14 June 2008, two police officers accompanied the applicant to the door leading out of the police station.
The applicant was able to take only a few steps after leaving Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 and then again lost consciousness.
At 5.20 p.m. on 14 June 2008 the applicant was admitted to hospital with the diagnosis of traumatic brain injury and contusion of the soft tissues around the nape of his neck.

According to the Government, on 14 June 2008 the police intervened in the gathering at the café on the basis of a complaint from people living in the neighbourhood of the café, who complained about noise and the behaviour of those attending.

The spokesman for the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Azerbaijan, E.Z., stated that on 14 June 2008 a group of people held an unauthorised gathering at a café and the police requested the interruption of the unauthorised gathering.
The Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009 found that the police intervention had been lawful, since the gathering at the café in the city centre disturbed other people present.

Article 4.1 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 of Azerbaijan, as in force at the material time, provided that the right to hold gatherings in places which are in private ownership is not regulated by that Law.

The Venice Commission Opinion no. 384/2006 stated that Article 4.1 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 of Azerbaijan, which provides that peaceful assemblies in places in private ownership shall not be regulated by the Law, is positive in that assemblies on private property are exempted from any notification requirement as well as from all other requirements provided for in the Law.

The Venice Commission Opinion no. 384/2006 stated that Article 4.1 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 of Azerbaijan shall not be interpreted as prohibiting spontaneous assemblies on private property, and that if the assembly is peaceful it should be allowed.
By a decision of 27 June 2008, the investigator refused to institute criminal proceedings, finding that there was no evidence that the applicant had been ill-treated by the police.
The applicant was not informed of the decision of 27 June 2008 concerning the investigator's refusal to institute criminal proceedings.

In his criminal complaint to the Nasimi District Court, the applicant pointed out that the investigator had questioned neither the police officers who had been involved in the alleged ill-treatment nor the other witnesses.
The applicant stated in his criminal complaint that he had not learned about the existence of the investigator's decision of 27 June 2008 until 3 March 2009.
On 31 March 2009 the Nasimi District Court dismissed the applicant's criminal complaint, finding the investigator's decision of 27 June 2008 lawful.
The Nasimi District Court's decision of 31 March 2009 was silent as to the applicant's particular complaints.

The Nasimi District Court's decision of 31 March 2009 found that the investigator had taken all necessary steps in carrying out a preliminary examination in compliance with Article 207 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and had adopted a justified and lawful decision on refusal to institute criminal proceedings.
In his appeal of 6 April 2009, the applicant complained that the investigator had not arranged an identity parade including police officer O.A.

In his appeal of 6 April 2009, the applicant complained that the investigator had not questioned the police officers involved in his arrest and detention, and in particular the Deputy Head of Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 in whose room and in whose presence he had allegedly been ill-treated.
In his appeal of 6 April 2009, the applicant complained that the investigator had failed to obtain video recordings from security cameras situated in Nasimi District Police Station no. 22.
In his appeal of 6 April 2009, the applicant disputed the conclusions of the forensic report dated 23 June 2008, pointing out that he had not been provided with a copy of it.
On 27 April 2009 the Baku Court of Appeal upheld the Nasimi District Court's decision of 31 March 2009.
On 25 July 2008 the Nasimi District Court refused to admit the applicant's civil action, finding that it did not comply with the procedural requirements for lodging a complaint.
On 2 September 2008 the Baku Court of Appeal upheld the Nasimi District Court's decision of 25 July 2008 refusing to admit the applicant's civil action.
On 17 November 2008 the Supreme Court of Azerbaijan quashed the Baku Court of Appeal's decision of 2 September 2008 and remitted the case to the lower courts for a new examination.
On 17 June 2009 the Nasimi District Court, having examined the applicant's civil action on the merits, decided to dismiss it.
The Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009 found that it had not been established that the applicant had been ill-treated by the police.

The Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009 noted that an investigator from Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 had examined the fact that the applicant had sustained injuries and had decided to refuse to institute criminal proceedings because no criminal act had been established, and that this decision had not been challenged.

The Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009 found that it was not established that the applicant had sustained a bodily injury or been subjected to physical violence, beaten or been under duress at the police station.
On 14 October 2009 the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal against the Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009.
On 7 May 2010 the Supreme Court of Azerbaijan upheld the lower courts' judgments in the civil proceedings.

In accordance with Article 212.2 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of Azerbaijan, any person providing information about a committed or planned criminal offence should be provided within twenty-four hours with a copy of the investigator's decision concerning refusal to institute criminal proceedings.
